### 💡 Codex Review Here are some automated review suggestions for this pull request. **Reviewed commit:** `d465107d9e`
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
[Your team has set up Codex to review pull requests in this repo](https://chatgpt.com/codex/cloud/settings/general). Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. Codex can also answer questions or update the PR. Try commenting "@codex address that feedback".

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize directory markers before protected-path validation**

When the planner follows the new prompt and emits an explicit directory such as `tests/`, this call passes the trailing slash to `isSentinelProtectedImplementationPath`, whose path validation treats the resulting empty final segment as protected. Consequently every supported directory scope is rejected as `plan_scope_invalid`, causing retries and eventual manual blocking instead of implementing issues that require a directory or new files; validate the normalized path while separately preventing directory scopes from covering protected controls.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce open dependencies before accepting a plan**

When an issue has an open `blockedBy` dependency, a planner can still return a schema-valid actionable finding and this validation accepts it without checking `job.relations.dependencies` or `dependenciesComplete`. The autonomous flow can therefore implement and deliver work that GitHub explicitly marks as blocked; reject incomplete dependency captures and deterministically persist an `unresolved_dependency` blocker whenever a captured prerequisite remains open.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate comment-count races to the affected queue item**

If a comment is added after `getIssue` returns but before `listIssueComments` completes, `current.comments` contains the old count while the captured list contains the new comment, so `materialContextDigest` throws at this call. Because the per-candidate loop does not retry or classify that consistency error as `source_unavailable`, one actively discussed issue aborts the entire workflow instead of allowing later eligible queue entries to be inspected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
